subject: Compute runbook: forecast & allocator confirmation for VelocitySys
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Li <ethan@velocitysys.ai>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 21 Jun 2028 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Compute runbook: forecast & allocator confirmation for VelocitySys

Hi Ethan —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. As we talked about, we're preparing a short compute runbook so your Prod launch (target week of Aug 7) has predictable latency and cost. Before I lock a provisional allocation, can you confirm the expected peak concurrent inference sessions and an example prompt length distribution? A quick table is fine: qps, avg tokens/input, peak sessions, expected start date.

Goal from our side: propose a compact dedicated pool (mix of A100 80GB + a couple of T4s for background tasks) and a small warm-up staging pool for onboarding. I want to run this by Ops to make sure there are no conflicts with other late-stage commitments during your launch window.

Attached a quick snapshot of our fleet utilization and a draft MoA we can use for the procurement conversation.

Next step: if you can send the usage numbers today, I'll circulate to ops and get a headcount for the allocator plan.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Account Executive
Redwood Inference
Attachments: capacity_snapshot_2028-06-20.csv (csv), velocitysys_moa_draft.pdf (pdf)
From: Ethan Li <ethan@velocitysys.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Jun 2028 11:14:23 -0700
Subject: Re: Compute runbook: forecast & allocator confirmation for VelocitySys

Chloe —

Thanks, sent the numbers below. We're aiming for a controlled rollout in early August, full traffic by Aug 21 if all goes well. Procurement looped in.

VelocitySys expected footprint (initial):
- QPS (avg): 25
- Concurrent inference sessions (peak): ~120
- Typical prompt tokens (avg): 320 tokens in, 280 tokens out
- Long tail: 5% of requests up to 2,000 tokens
- Expected start: Aug 7 internal beta; Aug 21 public

We prefer dedicated GPU for predictable latency. Happy to take a staging pool for the beta. Let me know if you need more granularity (batch sizes, warm/cold cache assumptions).

—Ethan
Ethan Li
Head of Platform
VelocitySys
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Jun 2028 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Compute runbook: forecast & allocator confirmation for VelocitySys

Hi team — forwarding customer numbers. Key asks: peak ~120 concurrent, avg QPS 25, 5% long-tail requests up to 2k tokens. They want a staging pool for Aug 7 and full traffic by Aug 21.

Can ops/allocations confirm feasibility for a provisional dedicated pool (estimate: 4x A100-80 + 2x T4 for background/embeddings) for the Aug 7–Sep 30 window? If we can't hold that exact shape, propose alternatives (e.g., 3x A100 + dynamic reroute to hosted for long-tail). Please respond with:
- Suggested pool sizing (gpu type + count)
- Any conflicting late-stage commitments Aug 1–31 that would block allocation
- Estimated lead time for locking capacity and procurement notes

Thanks,
Chloe

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Jun 2028 08:37:15 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Compute runbook: forecast & allocator confirmation for VelocitySys

Chloe / Ben / Monica —

Quick ops readout after looking at the fleet schedule and the snapshot you attached:
- Aug 7–31: we have several late-stage ramp commitments (HelioApps and Apexity) but there is a narrow window to carve out capacity if we act this week.
- Proposed provisional allocator: 3x A100-80 (primary inference) + 2x A40 (warm cache and embeddings) + 1x T4 (batch/sidecar). That should cover average load with headroom for spikes if we enforce a 16-token batch cap and enable prefix KV caching.
- Long-tail mitigation: route >1,000-token requests to hosted fallback model (slightly higher latency but safe), or we can add one temporary A100 if VelocitySys signs the provisional MoA by Friday.
- Lead time: We can pin the 3xA100 + 2xA40 pool as a soft hold for up to two weeks; hard reserving (contract & billing trigger) requires procurement paperwork and a commit.
- Conflicts: HelioApps has a soft hold on 2x A100 from Aug 12–25; if VelocitySys needs full traffic at Aug 21 there is a potential overlap — recommend negotiating a staggered ramp or a single extra A100 as insurance.

I'll coordinate a brief capacity table and escalation plan if we need to propose an embargos/transfer to Dedicated.

-rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Capacity Planning Lead
Redwood Inference
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Li <ethan@velocitysys.ai>, procurement@velocitysys.ai
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Jun 2028 17:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Compute runbook: forecast & allocator confirmation for VelocitySys

Ethan —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Based on ops feedback, here's a consolidated plan and the asks to move forward:

1) Provisional allocation (soft-hold): 3x A100-80 + 2x A40 + 1x T4 for Aug 7–Sep 30. Soft-hold window: 2 weeks.
2) Long-tail plan: route requests >1k tokens to hosted fallback; add 1x A100 as insurance if MoA is executed by 2028-06-28.
3) Next steps for VelocitySys: please review and sign the attached MoA (velocitysys_moa_draft.pdf) with a provisional start date Aug 7 and notify procurement. Signed MoA will trigger us to hard reserve the insurance A100 and extend the hold.
4) I'll kick off a quick runway call with Ops (Rishi & Monica) if you want to walk through the failover and caching assumptions.

If procurement needs a billing snapshot or a DocuSign, we've included links in the HubSpot deal.

Appreciate it — we'll do our best to keep the ramp smooth.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Account Executive
Redwood Inference
Attachments: velocitysys_moa_draft.pdf
